mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-17.4 to -8.9). This autoregressive momentum reflects an ongoing recovery trend that will persist, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite three prior consecutive weekly increases.

If this plateau persists, the associated lunch-hour and after-work retail traffic boost will stop accelerating, causing RETAIL_REC growth to flatten within two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved only -0.3 points from t-1w to t-0w after a large prior jump
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at a comparable or faster rate over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES growth has stalled.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-23.3 to -13.4) and WORKPLACES (-22.7 to -6.6) are improving together, jointly signaling restored commuting-linked routines. When both rise concurrently, combined errand-running and after-work shopping trips compound, driving RETAIL_REC higher faster than either series alone would predict over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than growth predicted from TRANSIT or WORKPLACES improving in isolation (i.e., no synergistic lift observed).

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 4.4 to 0.7, indicating people are spending progressively less time at home. In a reopening regime, this behavioral shift away from home-centric activity frees time for out-of-home discretionary spending, supporting continued RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell every week from 4.4 to 0.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, indicating the behavioral substitution mechanism does not hold outside a reopening regime.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is highly volatile and spikes above 50 points in weeks t-2w and t-0w, consistent with favorable weather drawing people outdoors. When PARKS spikes sharply, discretionary trips substitute toward outdoor leisure and away from indoor retail and recreation venues, temporarily suppressing RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 50.3 in the most recent week after dropping to 12.7 the week prior
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a PARKS reading above 45 points, contradicting the substitution effect.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 12.4 to 9.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next two weeks despite the observed GROCERY_PHARM deceleration.
